results: Reused and privately rebuilt the shared OrderedFiniteContinuity module from articles/kdv-convexity at its pinned recorded commit. Its three theorems and one definition prove continuity of finite ordered real entries from cumulative-count stability away from limiting entries,including repeated values. No source change was needed.

For the ACTUAL real original physical source spectrum,a real-diameter circle is in the full physical resolvent when its left endpoint is below the entire spectrum and its right endpoint is not spectral. The ACTUAL disk algebraic count is EXACTLY finiteLowerCount of the intrinsic canonical central prefix,including every full physical algebraic repetition. This is proved by finite double counting,not by assuming a supplied root list.

Every ACTUAL intrinsic canonical real label is now weak-star continuous on EVERY original endpoint norm-bounded physical set. The proof chooses one uniform norm-ball cutoff before the family,uses actual original spectral lower bounds,and applies the proved physical disk-count stability to the exact canonical cumulative counts. All repeated entries and closed gaps are included.

Every ACTUAL signed canonical gap is weak-star continuous on every bounded original physical set. The entire canonical label sequence and entire signed gap sequence are continuous in their product topologies. No continuity in the weighted infinity norm is asserted.

sourceCanonicalSpectralFiber prescribes the ENTIRE actual canonical spectrum with ALL algebraic repetitions. Such a fiber is relatively weak-star closed on EVERY bounded original physical set,and its intersection with each specified original endpoint norm ball is weak-star compact.

An ENTIRE original endpoint canonical spectral fiber is weak-star compact IFF it is bounded in the EXACT original endpoint norm. A globally bounded fiber is closed in the ENTIRE physical weak-star space. Actual spectrum exhaustion and all physical algebraic multiplicities are explicitly identified from the prescribed labels. Fiber membership is invariant under endpoint-order reinterpretation of the SAME entire original distribution.
